Question: How many different integers can be expressed as the sum of three distinct members of the set \(\{1,4,7,10,13,16,19\}?\)
Solution:
Each member of the set is one more than a multiple of \(3\). Adding three members therefore produces a multiple of \(3\). Because the members must be distinct, the smallest and largest possible sums are
\[
1+4+7=12,\qquad 13+16+19=48.
\]
Thus every possible sum belongs to the list
\[
12,15,18,\ldots,48,
\]
which contains
\[
\frac{48-12}{3}+1=13
\]
values. We still need to show that none of these values is missing.

Start with the triple \((1,4,7)\). Increase its largest entry by \(3\) at a time until it reaches \(19\). Next increase the middle entry by \(3\) at a time until it reaches \(16\). Finally increase the smallest entry by \(3\) at a time until it reaches \(13\).

Throughout this process, the entries remain distinct members of the original set. Every step increases the sum by exactly \(3\), and the process ends at \((13,16,19)\). It therefore attains every value from \(12\) through \(48\) in steps of \(3\), without repeating a sum along the way. The earlier bound excludes all other values.

There are exactly \(\boxed{13}\) different sums, choice A.
